title: OAuth login fails on headless VPS: "Premature close" fetching oauth2.googleapis.com/token (CLI HTTP stack only)

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides detailed environment information (gemini-cli v0.51.0, Node v22.23.0, Ubuntu 24.04 VPS), exact error traces ('Premature close' fetching oauth2.googleapis.com/token), and thorough isolation testing results showing that curl, Python, and raw Node fetch work on the same system while only the CLI bundle fails.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Investigating network stream premature close errors in Node/google-auth-library during OAuth token exchange across different network stack environments requires debugging HTTP transport options, retry logic, and asynchronous flow handling in packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts.

summary.problem: OAuth login fails with 'Premature close' error when requesting tokens from oauth2.googleapis.com in headless VPS environments.
summary.root_cause: The HTTP transport layer inside google-auth-library/OAuth2Client encounters stream premature closure when communicating with the token endpoint under specific Node.js HTTP stack/network configurations.
summary.context: Both browser redirect and NO_BROWSER=true user-code auth flows fail during token exchange with FatalAuthenticationError (exit code 41).

steps: Update OAuth2Client transport options in initOauthClient in packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts to handle HTTP request options and retry policies for token endpoint fetch operations.
Add error handling and retry logic around client.getToken calls in authWithUserCode and authWithWeb to gracefully handle premature connection closures.
Ensure cached credentials in OAuthCredentialStorage are appropriately validated and handled if re-authentication fails.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: OAuth token exchange completes successfully or retries transient transport errors, preventing FatalAuthenticationError caused by premature HTTP response stream closures.
verification_steps: Add unit tests mocking premature stream close responses on client.getToken to verify retry logic and proper exception handling.
